title: Vendor Access Provisioning & Approval Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the standard process, minimum controls, and approval criteria for granting, reviewing, and revoking third-party (vendor) access to Redwood Inference systems and data. It is tailored to short-lived operational access patterns often used by service providers, consultants, managed-support vendors, and hardware/infra partners.

Scope:
- Applies to all vendor or contractor requests for interactive access, API keys with elevated privileges, SSH/RDP access to host systems, access to model weights/artifacts, or long-running service accounts.
- Not intended for internal employee onboarding (see internal IAM playbook).

Principles:
- Least privilege by default. Grant the minimum role and narrowest resource scope required for the stated task.
- Time-boxed access with automated expiry. Manual perpetual credentials are disallowed unless explicit exception approved by Security+Legal.
- Auditability: All vendor sessions must be recorded or have telemetry sufficient to reconstruct actions per retention policy.
- Separation of duties for approval: Business sponsor (Data/Platform owner) must request; Security reviews risk and approves scope; SRE/Infra validates operational access steps.

Access tiers (example taxonomy):
- Tier 0: No access (vendor cannot access any production resources)
- Tier 1: Observability/Read-only telemetry (dashboards, aggregated metrics)
- Tier 2: Scoped read-only (logs for a named service, read-only buckets)
- Tier 3: Scoped write (upload artifacts to a restricted bucket, push artifacts to a staging model-hosting pool)
- Tier 4: Ephemeral operator (time-limited interactive SSH/adb/container exec for troubleshooting, session recording required)
- Tier 5: Elevated operations (ability to trigger deploys, modify routing) — exceptionally rare and requires exec-level sponsorship

Approval matrix (minimum approvers per tier):
- Tier 1: Business sponsor + Vendor admin contact
- Tier 2: Business sponsor + Security reviewer
- Tier 3: Business sponsor + Security reviewer + SRE approver
- Tier 4: Business sponsor + Security reviewer + SRE approver + On-call owner sign-off
- Tier 5: Business sponsor + Security reviewer + SRE approver + Legal + VP approval

Required artifacts for any access request (submit as part of onboarding JIRA ticket):
1) Business justification: who, why, expected success criteria, and observable metric to indicate access no longer needed.
2) Vendor details: company name, primary point-of-contact, contract reference, SOC/ISO attestations, and name of the engineer(s).
3) Scope specification: explicit resources, API endpoints, dataset names, cluster/node names, and permitted actions (read/list/write/execute).
4) Duration and revalidation cadence: requested duration (max 72 hours for Tier 4; 30 days for Tier 3; default 7 days for contractors unless extended) and revalidation recurrence.
5) Technical plan: how access will be performed (bastion, ephemeral cert, OAuth client), expected IP ranges, SAML/SCIM user mapping requests.
6) Audit & telemetry plan: session recording (if interactive), log collection endpoints, sampling rates, and retention label.
7) Rollback & escalation contacts: vendor escalation phone/email, Redwood on-call, remediation runbook reference.
8) Data protection checklist: whether PII or model weights are involved, required encryption at rest/in transit controls, and required pseudonymization.

Minimum security controls (baseline required):
- Identity: Use short-lived credentials (OIDC/OAuth tokens, short-lived certs) or SCIM-provisioned accounts with enforced MFA. Shared static credentials prohibited unless approved with compensating controls.
- Network: Access only via bastion/jump-host, VPN with context-aware rules, or private peering. Explicitly deny broad outbound if not required.
- Entitlements: Grant scoped IAM roles at resource level; avoid org-level roles.
- Session capture: For Tier 4+, all interactive sessions must be recorded and stored in the central evidence store with tags linking to the access ticket.
- Logging: Vendor actions must emit structured audit logs with user id, timestamp, resource, action, and request identifiers. Logs must be forwarded to SIEM with retention label vendor-access-evidence (default 90 days).
- Data handling: Any config, artifact or telemetry pulled by vendor must be handled under contract-approved DPA/annex with permitted uses and retention limits.

Temporary credentials lifecycle and automation: 
- Default request flow provisions credentials that expire at the requested end time. For ad-hoc emergency access, use a separate emergency access ticket with shortened approval SLAs and post-hoc attestation.
- Where possible, use ephemeral workloads (job-based access) rather than interactive accounts.
- Automate revocation: Tickets closed or expired automatically trigger deprovisioning hooks (SCIM delete, revoke token via identity provider API, rotate secrets).

Review & revalidation cadence:
- Tier 1/2: Quarterly automated revalidation by business sponsor.
- Tier 3: Monthly revalidation and evidence collected in ticket.
- Tier 4: Revalidation mandatory after any security incident and on every access event beyond the initial window.
- Any access older than the approved window is auto-revoked; extensions must follow the same approval flow.

Deprovisioning checklist (on ticket close or expiry):
- Confirm credentials revoked (identity provider logs)
- Confirm session recordings uploaded and linked to ticket
- Confirm all vendor-owned keys removed from build systems and secret stores
- Confirm any temporary storage bucket objects are cleaned or moved to approved retention zones
- Post-access questionnaire completed by business sponsor (one-liner: was access sufficient and safe?)

Audit-ready evidence artifacts (minimum to attach to ticket):
- Signed approval emails or ticket approvals from required approvers
- Identity provider issuance & revocation logs for the vendor identities
- Session recordings (if applicable) and index file with timestamps of high-risk commands/operations
- SIEM search snapshot that shows vendor actions during the window
- Post-access remediation notes (if cleanup required)

Exception handling & escalations:
- Exceptions to maximum durations or permanent accounts must be submitted as an "Access Exception" PR with business case and compensating controls; Security + Legal must approve.
- Emergency access: use the on-call emergency flow. Security must be notified within 60 minutes and a post-mortem ticket filed within 72 hours.

Sample approval justification snippet (templated):
"Requestor: Acme Ops (vendor) - Jane Doe
Business sponsor: Model Infra (owner: Priya Singh)
Scope: Read-only access to logs for model-hosting cluster 'model-prod-03' and upload permission to 'vendor-staging-bucket' for diagnostic artifacts.
Duration: 48 hours (2024-10-12 04:00 UTC to 2024-10-14 04:00 UTC)
Justification: Triaging inference latency spikes tied to quantized kernel rollout; vendor engineers will capture traces and upload diagnostics to restricted bucket.
Controls: Access via bastion only; session recording enabled; tokens issued via OIDC with 48h expiry; no access to model weights or training datasets.
Approvals: Business sponsor (Priya Singh) + Security reviewer (Laura Chen) + SRE approver (Jordan Mills)
"
